1. Use of at least one compound AB which is non-toxic to the skin chosen from NADH, NADPH, Cyt C (Fe2+) or H202 for measuring the status of oxidative stress of a biological matrix, characterized in that said at least one compound is available in two forms AB that do not interact with each other, and which are capable of interacting and/or forming complexes respectively with an antioxidant and an oxidant present on the surface or in said biological matrix.
2. Use according to claim 1, wherein at least two compounds AB are used simultaneously.
3. Device for measuring the total antioxidant/oxidizing power of a biological matrix comprising a measuring medium in which are immersed one or more working electrodes and one or more reference electrodes, characterized in that said medium comprises one at least one compound AB available in two forms A and B, which are capable of interacting and/or of forming complexes respectively with antioxidants and oxidants present at the surface or in the matrix, and not interacting with each other, and that said at least one compound AB is chosen from NADH, NADPH, Cyt C (Fe2+) or H202.
4. Device according to claim 3, wherein said one or more working electrodes is a complex electrode made of at least two materials selected from gold, platinum or tungsten.
5. Device according to one of claims 3 or 4, wherein the reference electrode is made of silver chloride and the working electrode is made of tungsten, platinum and gold.
6. Device according to one of claims 3 to 5, wherein said measuring medium is a solution of potassium chloride.
7. Method for measuring the status of oxidative stress of a biological matrix, characterized in that it comprises the steps of:
- bringing said matrix into contact with a measuring medium comprising at least one compound AB chosen from NADH, NADPH, Cyt C (Fe2+) or H202, available in two forms A and B which are capable of interacting and/or forming complexes respectively with an antioxidant and an oxidant present at the surface or in said matrix,
- measuring the electrochemical potential between a complex working electrode or several working electrodes and one or more reference electrodes placed on the matrix by electrochemistry, or measuring a variation in the absorbance by spectrophotometry.
8. Method according to claim 7, characterized in that said measuring medium is in liquid form or in gelled form.
9. Method according to claim 8, characterized in that at least two compounds AB are used simultaneously.
10. Method for determining the oxidative score of a biological matrix, characterized in that it comprises combining the results of at least two measurements chosen from:
- an electrochemical measurement measuring the total antioxidant/oxidizing power of said matrix by applying the method defined in one of claims
7 or 8,
- a spectrophotometric measurement measuring the anti-free radical effect and the reducing effect of said matrix, and
- a measurement by fluorimetry measuring the protective effect of said matrix.
11. Method according to claim 10, characterized in that it comprises both measuring said total antioxidant/oxidizing power of said anti-free radical effect, of said reducing effect and of said protective effect.
